key_insight: The paper asks when an open model can faithfully stand in for a closed one in mechanistic interpretability. It finds that surrogate fidelity depends on the level of analysis—prediction, attribution, or representation—and that simple API-accessible quantities like log-odds can sometimes serve as reliable readouts for binary tasks.
problem_solved: Mechanistic interpretability usually needs full model internals, but most deployed LLMs only expose limited APIs. This paper addresses the surrogate problem: how to draw valid conclusions about a closed model using measurements from an open surrogate model.
method: Evaluate surrogate fidelity at three levels: prediction, attribution, and representation.
Compare how well open-model measurements transfer to closed-model behavior under API constraints.
Use log-odds as an API-compatible scalar readout for binary classification settings.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners know when open models can be used as stand-ins for closed models in interpretability studies. It can reduce reliance on inaccessible systems while improving the reliability of conclusions drawn from model behavior.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram showing closed model vs open surrogate model
Three-layer schematic for prediction, attribution, and representation fidelity
Simple bar chart or heatmap comparing fidelity across analysis levels
Icon set for API access, log-odds, and model internals
paper_title: Surrogate Fidelity: When Can Open LLMs Explain Closed Ones?
paper_authors: Philippe Chlenski, Zachariah Carmichael, Ayush Warikoo, Chia-Tse Shao, Yingxiao Ye
